opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Black (employee ID E008) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E008.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Karen Black (E008) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin on Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and she does not own it, so admin is not permitted. Maximum for full-time employees without ownership is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E008 (Karen Black) is a contractor with basic security training (note: prior note listed full-time, but security record says contractor). Contractors with basic training max out at read; never admin. She requested admin on Source Code, so recommend read.
reason: Karen Black (E008) requested admin access to Source Code. The Security agent's note indicates the security DB lists her as a contractor with basic security training (flagging that the HR note listing full-time is inconsistent with the security record). Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and as a Payroll Specialist she does not own it. Contractors are never admin; with only basic training, the maximum permitted level is read. Since requested admin exceeds the maximum, grant the maximum of read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Karen Black (E008)
Request: admin access to Source Code

Team memory has two notes with conflicting information:
- HR note: full_time Payroll Specialist, recommendation write
- Security note: contractor, basic security training, recommendation read

The notes conflict on employment type. HR says full_time, Security says contractor (and notes the discrepancy).

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

Source Code is owned by the Engineer role. Karen is a Payroll Specialist, so she doesn't own it.

If full_time: max is write (no ownership). Requested admin > write, so grant write.
If contractor: basic training, max is read. Requested admin > read, so grant read.

The conflict matters: write vs read.

How to resolve? The Security agent's note specifically flags that the security record says contractor, "note: prior note listed full-time, but security record says contractor". Security records are probably more authoritative for employment type? Hmm. The team memory approach: both agents write notes with facts they have. The Approver reads the notes and makes the final decision.

Which to trust? The Security agent explicitly flagged the discrepancy and said security DB says contractor. Security DB is likely the authoritative source for employment type/security training. So I'll go with contractor with basic training → max read.

Requested admin > read, so grant read.

Let me submit decision: read.
